why: The storm's wave crest turns into a glowing teal chart line that peels back to reveal a classroom bench: a clever 'markets as sea' idea I'd scroll to see finish. But the heading says '3 IDIOTS / The Workshop' while the caption still says 'THE KRAKEN'S STORM · PIRATES OF THE CARIBBEAN', so for a moment I didn't know which act I was in.

A burning hole opening in the middle of the RDR camp with a lone candle flame inside is a real cinematic 'what's on the other side?' moment. The 'HARRY POTTER' heading above an RDR plate and an RDR caption is confusing for a beat.

About 70% of the frame is flat black with a title top-left and a small porthole of the ship bottom-right. It reads as an image that hasn't loaded rather than an iris opening; nothing pulls the eye to the middle.

A jagged white tear, lightning-like, splits a misty classroom from a teal storm sea; dramatic and clearly mid-transition. The act heading and the plate caption still name different worlds (3 Idiots vs Pirates).
Strong western wood-type title over a sepia tintype in a cream mount feels like an old photograph being handed to you; calm but confident, and the horse in the valley invites a closer look.
Same as H005 (only the egg counter moved to 1/12). Handsome; the egg counter changing quietly makes me want to know what I found.

Better than H003: the gold ring is brighter and the sea and ship are starting to bleed in behind it, so it reads as a porthole/iris opening rather than an empty page. Still a lot of dead space on the left.
The burn hole is wider and the edge glows hotter; it clearly promises a jump into the next world. The heading/caption mismatch ('HARRY POTTER' over 'THE CAMPFIRE · RED DEAD REDEMPTION 2') remains.
